utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, will you please call the case?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is case number IT-95-10-A, Prosecutor versus Goran Jelisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Jelisic, can you hear me? Mr. Jelisic says yes, he can hear me. Now, I should explain that under Rule 65 bis, these proceedings can be held either by the whole Appeals Chamber or by a Judge of the Appeals Chamber, and as you will see, a single Judge is sitting today. I take it that you would appreciate that that in no way diminishes the authority or status of our proceedings today. Now, may I take the appearances, first the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: May it please, Your Honour. Upawansa Yapa appearing for the Prosecution, with Mr. Norman Farrell and Mr. Roeland Bos. Ms. Carmela Annink-Javier is the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: For the Appellant/Defence. Perhaps I should have asked. There is only the Defence is appealing in this case, is that right, or is the Prosecution also appealing?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: You're also appealing. So, Defence/Appellant.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I appear on behalf of the appellant. My name is Michael Greaves, and I have with me today Mr. Michael Levy from the bar of England and Wales. Your Honour, could I just mention one thing, to see Your Honour's leave to have sitting with us our interpreter. Neither Mr. Levy not I speak the language of Mr. Jelisic, and we need to take instructions in the course of this hearing, we will need to speak through an interpreter. May I have Your Honour's leave to have her sit with us, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Yapa, I take that it there is no opposition to this request which repeats a request made on the last occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: No objection whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: That is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'm most grateful to Your Honour. I, therefore, introduce to Your Honour Ms. Ratislava Mirkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, may I just read the applicable Rule which controls our proceedings this afternoon. It is Rule 65 bis and it says: "The Appeals Chamber or an Appeals Chamber Judge shall convene a Status Conference within one hundred and twenty days of the filing of a notice of appeal and thereafter within one hundred and twenty days after the last Status Conference to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and the physical condition of that person." The last Status Conference was held on the 4th of April, and that Status Conference visualised a second Status Conference could be held at or around the second week of July this year, and on the 12th of April, 2000, we issued a scheduling order summoning this Status Conference for today. Now, the purposes of the conference have been read out in brief. They are to afford to the appellant an opportunity to make any representations about his conditions of detention or any representations about his appeal, the status of his appeal, and also to give to the Court an opportunity to indicate the position regarding the prospect of the appeal being heard. So now, are there any representations, Mr. Greaves?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's nothing in particular that I would wish to address Your Honour sitting alone on. Of course, there is the matter of the request for an extension of time, but that's a matter that all five Judges of the Appeals Chamber are seized of, so it would not be proper of me, at this stage, to address Your Honour in any way on that, so I don't. Beyond that, I have no other observations to make either about the appellant or his conditions of detention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. Very good of you, Mr. Greaves, to recognise the limitations on the competence of a single Judge. But we can notice, can we not, that the Prosecution was asked to respond to that motion, and the Prosecution has responded?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: We have. We have responded, Your Honour, and also we have filed our brief in appeal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Now, that motion brings me to this point, Mr. Greaves: that we have in the interval since the end of the trial in the Trial Chamber had a series of motions for extensions of time and that has occupied this space between the termination of the proceedings in the Trial Chamber and today's date, and that affects the prospect of the appeal coming on for hearing. We have in mind that the appeal would come on for hearing very shortly after the beginning of September/October, somewhere there. Would that meet with your expectations, Mr. Greaves?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honours, certainly bearing in mind what Your Honours said on the last occasion, that is something that we've been working, as it were, towards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. Should we hear from Mr. Jelisic himself, if he has any particular thing to say to the Court?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it is usual to ask the appellant himself personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Very good of you, Mr. Greaves. Then, Mr. Jelisic, would you like to say whether you have any particular representation to make to the Court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: You accept what Mr. Greaves has said? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Is there anything you would like to add to what Mr. Greaves has said? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] I don't understand these matters so well. I don't know what he explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, then, do I take it that you have confidence in Mr. Greaves and in what he would have said on your behalf? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely, I do have confidence, and whatever you agree with my counsel, I accept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Shall we, then, note that the present state of affairs is controlled by the pendency of a motion for extension of time, and that subject to that our anticipation is that the hearing of the appeal would take place sometime in September/October coming. Unless, then, there are other matters to be discussed, may I suggest that we now take the adjournment. Thank you.
